findings.title: Empty updateMany throws after cache is written
findings.body: fetchAvailabilityAndSetCache now ends with SelectedCalendarRepository.updateManyByCredentialId(this.credential.id, {}). Prisma Client rejects an empty updateMany data object (Argument data must not be empty) with PrismaClientValidationError, so the method throws after CalendarCache rows have already been upserted. unwatchCalendar in this same class awaits that call after it has already stopped Google watches, cleared channel fields, and deleted cache, so unwatch now fails even though the remaining calendars' cache was rewritten. Webhook-driven refresh uses this method too; a non-2xx response makes Google retry, re-query the Calendar API, and hit the same throw on every notification. An empty update would also not bump @updatedAt even if it were accepted, so the comment's intent is not met. This PR's UI reads CalendarCache.updatedAt, not SelectedCalendar.updatedAt, so the call looks unnecessary. Remove it, or if a touch is required pass { updatedAt: new Date() }. The new helper also types data as Prisma.SelectedCalendarUpdateInput, which is not the UpdateManyMutationInput updateMany accepts, so the helper can fail typecheck as well.

findings.title: Cache delete never refreshes connected calendars
findings.body: deleteCache.useMutation only toasts and calls the optional onSuccess prop. The disconnect mutation in the same component invalidates viewer.calendars.connectedCalendars and viewer.apps.integrations in onSettled; delete does not. SelectedCalendarsSettingsWebWrapper owns the connectedCalendars query and passes its optional onChanged through as onSuccess, without refetching that query. After a successful delete the menu still shows the previous cacheUpdatedAt and the Delete cached data action, so the UI contradicts the success toast. Delete also only runs calendarCache.deleteMany and leaves Google watch channels active, so a later webhook can insert a new row before the user reloads. Invalidate connectedCalendars in onSettled the same way disconnect does.

findings.title: Existing cache rows all get the migration timestamp
findings.body: updatedAt is added as NOT NULL DEFAULT NOW(), so every existing CalendarCache row is stamped with the migration time instead of the last real cache write. getCacheStatusByCredentialIds returns MAX(updatedAt) and the new menu shows it as Last updated. Right after deploy, every Google credential with any cache row looks freshly synced, including expired rows, because the status query does not filter expiresAt. That makes the status feature wrong for all current data until the next upsert. The header comment is also false: it says a required column without a default cannot be added to a non-empty table, but the SQL does set a default, which can make an operator abort a production migrate. Backfill from a real proxy (expiresAt minus the 30-day CACHING_TIME used when writing the cache) and correct the comment. NOW() is not a constant default, so PostgreSQL must rewrite CalendarCache under AccessExclusiveLock rather than using the instant add-column path, which blocks cache reads and writes for the length of the rewrite.

findings.title: UserWithCalendars requires fields this function never reads
findings.body: UserWithCalendars now requires updatedAt and googleChannelId on allSelectedCalendars and userLevelSelectedCalendars, but getConnectedDestinationCalendarsAndEnsureDefaultsInDb never reads either field. The function is exported, including the legacy getConnectedDestinationCalendars alias documented for @calcom/platform-libraries, so callers that previously passed selected calendars with only externalId, integration, and eventTypeId no longer typecheck. The only caller updated here is UserRepository.findUnlockedUserForSession, which now selects googleChannelId (the internal Google push-channel id) into the session user on every authenticated load just to satisfy the wider Pick. Drop the new required fields and the session select unless something in this change actually consumes them.

findings.title: Webhook script writes the wrong env file and breaks on Linux
findings.body: ENV_FILE is ../.env relative to the process cwd, not the script directory. bash scripts/test-gcal-webhooks.sh from the repo root therefore creates or edits a .env outside the repository and never sets GOOGLE_WEBHOOK_URL for the app, then prints success. The edit on line 68 uses sed -i '', which is BSD/macOS-only; GNU sed treats '' as the script and fails the substitution. set -e is off, and cleanup always exits 0, so a missing tunnel URL, the Tunnelmole rate limit, and a failed sed all look successful. Resolve the env path from the script directory and use a portable in-place edit.

findings.title: Cache delete authorization has no tests
findings.body: deleteCacheHandler is a new mutation whose only authorization is credential.findFirst({ id: credentialId, userId: user.id }) before calendarCache.deleteMany({ where: { credentialId } }). This PR adds no tests. Dropping or widening that filter would let any logged-in user wipe another user's calendar cache by credential id, and nothing checks that a non-owner is rejected, that only that credential's rows are removed, or that connectedCalendars actually attaches cacheUpdatedAt from getCacheStatusByCredentialIds. Add allow and deny handler tests before shipping the endpoint.

findings.title: dev:cron switched to undeclared tsx via npx
findings.body: dev:cron changed from ts-node cron-tester.ts to npx tsx cron-tester.ts. ts-node is a declared devDependency of @calcom/web; tsx is not. Under Yarn Berry, npx can skip the workspace install, prompt to download an arbitrary latest tsx, or fail non-interactively. This unrelated change regresses yarn dev:cron. Revert it, or add tsx as a dependency and run it through Yarn.

findings.title: Cache timestamp is always formatted en-US
findings.body: The only user-visible cache status value is formatted with new Intl.DateTimeFormat("en-US", { dateStyle: "short", timeStyle: "short" }). The component already calls useLocale(), but the timestamp ignores the active locale and the user's 12/24-hour time format, so every non-US user sees a US short date and a 12-hour clock in Last updated. Format with the current i18n locale and the user's time format instead of a hardcoded en-US formatter.
